tips.title: Aligning Wings with a Tamiya Jig
tips.text: For Trumpeter or Meng kits with large wing surfaces, use a Tamiya Wing Alignment Jig. Glue one wing half to the jig, align the other half on top, and apply cement. Let cure for 30 minutes, then carefully remove the jig. Ensure both wings are even using a straight edge, then glue to the fuselage.

tips.title: Assembling Multi-Part Gun Barrels (AFV Club)
tips.text: For AFV Club's detailed gun barrels, dry-fit parts first. Use Tamiya Extra Thin Cement for small parts; let cure for 15 minutes. Glue the smallest parts first, using tweezers, then work up to larger parts. For the final step, apply cement to the barrel's exterior seam, let cure for 30 minutes, then sand smooth with 400 grit.

tips.title: Installing Eduard Photo-Etch Parts
tips.text: Soak Eduard photo-etch parts in warm water for 10 seconds to soften. Remove, pat dry, and bend parts over a GodHand Nippers tip to shape. Use Eduard's CA Glue for tiny parts; apply a drop, let cure for 15 seconds, then attach the part. For larger parts, use Tamiya Extra Thin Cement and tweezers.

tips.title: Working with Resin Conversion Kits (Clear Prop Models)
tips.text: Pin-vice drill Clear Prop Models' resin parts at recommended locations. Assemble dry, using CA glue for joins. Let cure for 30 minutes. Sand seams with 240 grit, then 400 grit. Clean parts with warm water, pat dry, and apply a thin layer of Vallejo Plastic Putty. Let dry, sand smooth, and prepare for painting.

tips.title: Strengthening Thin Parts with Brass Rod
tips.text: Reinforce ICM's 1/48 MiG-15bis' thin wing struts with brass rod (0.5mm). Cut rod to length, leaving extra for bending. Drill holes in the struts using the smallest bit that won't split the plastic. Superglue the brass rod into the holes, let cure for 1 hour. Trim excess brass with flush cutters, then sand smooth.
